bullets.text: Repurchased 16.9M shares via $1.5B tender offer at $88/share plus 1.7M shares open-market; invested assets $13.1B; total return 5.2%; debt-to-total capital ended at 20%; subsidiary operating leverage reached 2.9 premiums-to-surplus.

Declining accident frequency and widespread competitor profitability reduced consumer shopping; auto industry NPW growth slowed to an estimated 3.7%; top 15 auto insurers (72% share) outperformed industry in growth and profitability.

Temporarily reassessed maximum-growth goals to maintain relatively robust margins without significantly impairing growth. Selective rate actions favored rate stability, recognizing certain potential reductions would simply reduce margins with little volume change.

Net income rose 31% to a record $1.65 billion ($7.63 per share), driven by exceptional underwriting profitability. Progressive estimated the auto industry achieved perhaps its lowest combined ratio in history in 2004.

Net premiums written grew 12% (~$1.5B), meeting expectations of several times industry average growth. Direct Business grew 16.5%, the fastest among the top 15 competitors, and Agency Business grew 9.5%, ranking fifth.

Announced 'Drive Insurance from Progressive' for independent agents and brokers, advancing the initiative to create two top-share personal auto brands. The agency brand will be promoted via television, Yellow Pages, and other advertising.

Customer retention improvements in 2004 missed expectations for degree and speed, causing disappointment. Management recognized that methods for estimating customer relationship life expectancy under varying market conditions were not yet fully developed.

Expects 2005 New Jersey auto filings assuming proposed ratemaking regulations are promulgated. Operated 20 concierge claims centers and tested offering replacement vehicles instead of payments for un-repairable cars ahead of planned 2005 expansion.

Replaced billing system and began deploying an improved claims management platform. Planned 2005 progress includes improved customer management systems and IT infrastructure to enhance system availability and disaster preparedness.

Responded to four Southeastern hurricanes (Charley, Frances, Ivan, Jeanne). With nationwide assistance across all company areas, employees—many facing their own storm-related problems—managed claims relatively seamlessly and resolved them quickly.
